EICMA 2026 • Honda Africa Twin Gets Biggest Refresh in a Decade, They Now Call It CRF1150L
Get the Hen Dentist: 1987 Callaway Corvette Parked in Garage Is Out for the First Time Since 1999
36 photos
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins
What is the most famous overlooked Corvette out there? What factory-backed American sports car rewrote the performance rulebook in the 1980s while looking almost indistinguishable from a stock showroom cruiser? The Callaway Corvette would probably take first place, earning the most undeserved distinction ever: the champion of “Oh, THAT!” Speaking of which, here’s one to refresh your memory.
Built by Reeves Callaway and his engineering team in Old Lyme, Connecticut, the twin-turbocharged fourth-generation Corvette transformed Chevrolet's fiberglass two-seater into a world-class European supercar slayer. To this day, it is the fastest Corvette sold by Chevrolet, unless you can name another that has gone 254 miles per hour. Alright, the one-off Sledgehammer was not exactly a regular twin-turbo Callaway Corvette, but it was still street legal.
Founded in 1977 by former Bondurant racing instructor Reeves Callaway, Callaway Cars initially gained acclaim by engineering aftermarket turbocharger kits for Alfa Romeo, BMW, Porsche, and Mercedes-Benz models. After a twin-turbocharged Callaway Alfa Romeo GTV6 impressed Corvette Chief Engineer Dave McLellan, General Motors took the unprecedented step of assigning Regular Production Option code B2K to an outside specialist for 1987, backing the conversion with a factory warranty.
Available through select Chevrolet dealerships from 1987 to 1991, the RPO B2K Callaway Twin Turbo Corvette saw roughly 510 examples built across 5 model years. The program achieved global fame on October 26, 1988, when John Lingenfelter piloted the one-off, 880-hp Callaway Sledgehammer to a 254.76 mph world record for street-legal cars.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins If those 409 kph weren’t awesome enough, remember that Lingenfelter drove to car to Ohio's 7.5-mile Transportation Research Center oval 700 miles from Old Lyme, Connecticut. After mopping the floor with absolutely everyone else in the high-speed business, the Sledgehammer turned around and made the return trip on its wheels. Does it sound familiar? The ZR1X is scalping hypercars today for a fraction of the price.
But the other Callaway Corvettes were nothing to laugh at, either. A surviving piece of that first-year B2K history recently emerged from a 28-year slumber, because what better way to mark 40 years since the debut of the moniker if not with a garage find?
Dennis Collins, accompanied by mechanic sidekick Alex Bohling and cameraman Zach Gorgas, traveled before dawn to Grapevine, Texas, to meet owner Dave McGuire and purchase a 1987 Callaway Twin Turbo Corvette coupe parked in 1999, attested by the windshield registration stickers.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Authenticated by its dash plaque as car number 80 of 184 built for 1987, McGuire's coupe still wears its Texas vanity license plate reading B2K. Collins even brought along his own 1980s Texas dealer plate stamped B9P, the factory code for the 1988 Corvette Challenge race cars. The glovebox Service Parts Identification label confirms code B2K alongside Flame Red Metallic paint code 8748 over code 122 Graphite Gray leather upholstery.
While Collins and McGuire speculated that coupes were rarer than convertibles in 1987, factory records show 121 coupes and 63 convertibles comprised the 184-car run. Original warranty documents reveal that car number 80 was delivered new through Chalmers Chevrolet in Tulsa, Oklahoma, with 509 test miles on the clock. McGuire acquired the Corvette in 1995 from dealer Wes Abendroth in Colleyville, Texas, regrettably trading a 1967 Corvette Roadster straight across.
Before parking the car with 19,888 miles showing on the odometer, McGuire drove it hard and even drag raced a 1987 Buick GNX at the Texas Motorplex in Ennis. The quicker-launching Buick narrowly won the quarter-mile sprint before the 178 mph Callaway could reel it in. After buying the car despite a stuck hood cable, Collins opened the clamshell at his shop, uncovering Reeves Callaway's faint signature on the plenum.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins What makes an early 1987 Callaway Twin Turbo so deceptively anonymous compared to a standard Corvette is its restrained exterior. Because the 17-inch Dymag magnesium wheels and Paul Deutschman's sculpted AeroBody kit arrived later, early 1987 cars rolled on stock 16-inch alloys. Only twin NACA hood ducts, discreet Callaway emblems on the nose, B-pillars, and tail, and a Callaway Twin Turbo decal on the rear hatch glass betrayed its identity.
Inside the cockpit, Callaway added a round analog boost gauge in the center dash, a serialized brass console plaque, a 91-to-93 octane warning plate, and a spiral-bound Callaway owner's manual supplement. That exclusivity carried a staggering price tag in 1987. While a base Corvette coupe cost $27,999 and a convertible started at $33,172, selecting RPO code B2K added $19,995, pushing a loaded coupe like McGuire's between $48,500 and $52,585 new.
To justify that premium, fully assembled Corvettes were shipped from Bowling Green, Kentucky, to Old Lyme for over 100 mechanical modifications. While a stock 1987 L98 5.7-liter Tuned Port Injection V8 produced 240 hp and 345 lb-ft of torque, Callaway tore the 350-cubic-inch iron small-block completely down to its bare casting, machining four-bolt main bearing caps and installing a Nitrited crankshaft, forged connecting rods, and low-compression 7.5:1 forged Mahle pistons.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Two water-cooled IHI RHB6 turbochargers fed pressurized air through dual air-to-air intercoolers perched atop the valve covers, while a Callaway Micro-Fueler controller triggered two supplemental fuel injectors once boost reached 2 psi. Callaway also mandated Mobil 1 15W-50 synthetic motor oil. Every 1987 B2K Corvette channeled power through a Doug Nash 4+3 manual transmission, combining a 4-speed gearbox with an electronic overdrive unit operating on the top three gear ratios.
With 10 psi of boost, the 1987 Callaway V8 delivered 345 hp at 4,000 rpm, 465 lb-ft at 2,500 rpm, and a claimed 177.9 mph top speed. In period road tests, Car and Driver clocked 0 to 60 mph in 4.7 seconds, 100 mph in 11.6 seconds, and a 13.2-second quarter-mile at 108 mph, while Road and Track logged 5.0 seconds to 60 mph and 13.7 seconds at 104 mph.
Output climbed to 382 hp and 562 lb-ft in 1988 and reached 403 hp and 575 lb-ft by 1991, accompanied by a four-speed automatic option in 1988 and a ZF six-speed manual in 1989. Yet the 1987 cars remain the purest genesis of the RPO B2K legend. Having spent its life in Oklahoma and Texas, car number 80 now awaits a mechanical revival to put it back on the road.

5 New Hot Wheels Toyotas for Your Silver Series Collection
17 photos
Photo: Diecast Wheels
I just met another FC RX-7 owner yesterday. He messaged me last week that he might be in my area for a few days. And I just knew I had to give him a tour of the Transalpina touge. After all, he’s a big Initial D fan himself and he drove almost 20 hours to visit me.
I initially wanted to use my Mazda RX-8 for the trip, but it’s still on summer, semi-slick tires which just won’t work in the snow or freezing cold. We went with my station wagon instead, and the car wasn’t very happy with my driving. But that’s not what I wanted to talk about today. We stopped to get coffee at one point and I said: “Look, this is where I shop for Hot Wheels all the time.”
The guy’s face lit up immediately, and I realized he wanted a closer look, too. Our common passion for cars (big or tiny) brought us together, and we felt like old friends from the first few minutes. That alone is a good enough reason to start collecting Hot Wheels , regardless of what series they’re part of.
Right now, I’d like to show you the second preview of next year’s Silver Series Anniversary set that has five Toyota cars inside. We have seen a shot of it during a presentation at the 40th Annual Hot Wheels Collectors Convention in Los Angeles last month, but these new photos are a bit more relevant.
You’ll also notice some shots of the upcoming Car Culture: 2-Packs in the gallery: the card art on the Audi set is in perfect tone with the weather outside, isn’t it? The Toyota T100 Baja Truck is #1 of 5 for the mix, and you might remember this was originally a 100% release a quarter of a century ago. I took photos of the Auto Affinity variation for one of my unboxing stories earlier this year .
Phil Riehlman’s design has gone through a few changes since, and 2025 marked its first Silver Series variation for a similar Toyota set. It had a ZAMAC body then, and it’s safe to assume it will have one in 2027 as well. The 1970 Celica is #2 for the mix, and I admit I would have loved it if Mattel used the 1977 version instead.
Rob Matthes designed the latter, and it only showed up once in Car Culture so far. Meanwhile, Jun Imai created the 1970 Celica over a decade ago, with 11 variations coming out of El Segundo since. Look for The Hot Ones iteration from 2025 for a serious dose of nostalgia! The Toyota Land Cruiser 80 is bound to be a pretty popular choice, and at this point collecting Land Cruisers could be a side-quest on its own.
The Metalflake Green finish on this SUV looked amazing in 2025 and I regret not buying it: this new Toyota TRD-themed livery isn’t half bad either. We haven’t seen an individually-packed 2000GT since the 2024 Vintage Racing Club set. Despite its age, this casting feels timeless. It would be great if we got another Premium version of it soon, though.
I’m trying to figure out what wheels the new iteration is rolling on, but I’m having a hard time identifying the design. As much as I love the Star 5-Spoke look, these new wheels fit the theme a bit better. The 1981 Toyota Starlet is the final item in the set, and the one with the most interesting design from my perspective.
Well, I’m naturally drawn to it as I’ve wanted to drive one for many years now. Looking back at the four variations Mattel has released so far, I’m convinced I should try to get them all under the same roof as soon as possible. This Toyota mix should arrive in toy stores within the next few months. I doubt you’ll have a hard time getting any of the cars inside, but you know what they say: pre-ordering can be a great solution!

Photo: Rinnai
Rinnai has launched a new lineup of electric heat pump water heaters that adds wifi controls and more installation options to an appliance that can cut the energy needed for hot showers.
The REHPW series comes in 50-, 65-, and 80-gallon sizes. It builds on Rinnai’s existing REHP lineup, with changes designed to make the units easier to install, monitor, and maintain.
Hot water with less electricity
Heat pump water heaters pull heat from the surrounding air and transfer it into the tank. Moving that heat requires less electricity than producing it with conventional electric resistance elements. There’s no fuel combustion at the appliance, although emissions from its electricity supply depend on the grid.
Rinnai lists a Uniform Energy Factor, or UEF, of 3.75 for the 50-gallon model and 4.0 for the two larger versions. Higher numbers mean greater efficiency under standardized testing; actual bills depend on electricity rates, hot water use, and installation conditions.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The lineup delivers up to 91 gallons of hot water in the first hour, depending on tank size. That rating includes both stored hot water and what the unit can heat during that hour – useful context when several people take consecutive showers.
There are five operating modes, 4.5 kW backup heating elements, and a variable-speed fan designed to keep noise down. The heat pump can operate with ambient air as low as 37°F.
More ways to fit it in
Installation is where some of the more practical upgrades show up.
The new Rinnai heat pump water heater units have water connections on both the top and side, giving installers more options for connecting existing plumbing. Both the air intake and exhaust are on top, allowing zero side clearance where Rinnai’s installation requirements permit.
An optional ducting kit adds flexibility for tighter spaces. Carrying handles help with moving the tank into place, and the air filter slides out horizontally from the side for cleaning.
Rinnai has also added a third tank temperature sensor to the 50- and 80-gallon models to help manage hot water delivery.
Smarter controls and potential utility rebates
Wifi adds remote monitoring and control. Rinnai’s updated Central app supports the REHPW series, including scheduling and tools to use time-of-use electricity rates to manage energy use.
The units also carry CTA-2045 AC Level 2 certification for demand response. That gives compatible utility programs a way to communicate with the water heater and adjust its electricity use. Rinnai says the certification can help qualify homeowners for local and state utility demand-response rebates; availability depends on the program.
The series is Energy Star certified, meets NEEA Tier 4 requirements, and complies with California’s Title 24 requirements, including JA13, according to Rinnai. Warranty coverage includes 10 years for the tank and other parts, plus one year for labor.
Rinnai directs buyers to an installer for pricing, so the upfront cost – and how much a local rebate might offset it – will require a quote. However, the REHP series price on Amazon hovers around the $2,000 mark.

World, Say Hello to This Just-Restored Chevy Bel Air, Too Bad for the Engine
23 photos
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1
Sure, the Bel Air rapidly became plan B once the Impala debuted in 1958 , but this model continued to be a popular choice for many Americans. This 1961 specimen is here specifically with this goal in mind: it’s trying to demonstrate this to the audience, and it uses a freshly restored setup to do it.
The car looks to be in spotless shape, and as far as I’m concerned, the only reason to walk away is the engine under the hood.
The dealer trying to sell the car says the owner added only 500 miles since the engine was rebuilt, so whoever buys this Bel Air will almost literally drive a new car.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 The Bel Air was the model that brought home the bacon for Chevrolet throughout the ‘50s. This all changed when the GM brand introduced the Impala in 1958, first as a Bel Air version and eventually as a stand-alone series beginning in 1959. The Impala was the top-of-the-range model, and while the Bel Air adopted the same styling and engine lineup, it didn’t have all the bells and whistles of its more expensive brother.
The 1961 model year didn’t produce any change in this strategy. The Bel Air continued to be the backup plan for buyers who didn’t want to spend high dollars on an Impala, though Chevrolet tried to make the downgrade a more difficult decision.
1961 was the year when Chevrolet introduced the Super Sport, a $53.80 package that eventually became an iconic name in the automotive world. At the same time, the 1961 release also witnessed the introduction of the bubble top, a design that also made its way to the Bel Air.
From an engine perspective, things didn’t change much for Chevrolet’s full-size family. A six was still the base configuration, while the 283 Turbo-Fire continued to be the base V8 choice. The big news was the introduction of an actual big-block unit, with the 409 joining this year’s offering in February. It was a fantastic choice for the Super Sport, despite SS buyers not initially considering a more powerful engine as must-haves.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 A six isn’t necessarily the most desirable engine on a full-size Chevy, and this is why I believe that the 235ci unit on this car could be a reason for some potential buyers to walk away.
It has already been rebuilt, so it starts, runs, and drives beautifully. It is paired with an automatic transmission, and considering everything is in tip-top shape, you shouldn’t spend more dollars on preparing the vehicle for the road.
If you’re specifically interested in an all-original Bel Air, I believe that you’ll have to search somewhere else. The owner doesn’t offer more data on this front, and while there’s a good chance that the engine is the factory-installed unit, I wouldn’t be surprised to learn that the car has already received lots of changes.
For example, the paint isn’t original, but I do think that it looks good. The green finish aligns nicely with the turquoise interior, so maybe the photos don’t do enough justice to this Bel Air. An in-person inspection should help you figure out more details, though.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 As for the condition of the metal, there’s no rust on this Bel Air. The seller doesn’t offer more specifics as to how many repairs the vehicle has already received, especially on the underside, so maybe you should raise it on a lift to check the floors before making an offer.
To be honest, I don’t expect this Bel Air to remain available for long, especially because it seems to qualify as a fantastic choice for a daily driver. The seller advertises “numerous new parts” that have already been installed, with an overall mileage of close to 45,000 miles.
The six and the simple fact that it’s not an Impala make this Bel Air less valuable, and I think that every collector out there knows this very well. On the other hand, there’s no doubt that this Bel Air would be a great companion, especially for people who want to drive a classic on a sunny Sunday.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 The price is the thing that always makes the difference, and given the six under the hood and the changes it has already received, the $25,000 price tag makes perfect sense. The owner has also enabled the Make Offer option, so maybe you will be able to save a few dollars with the right negotiation skills.
The vehicle is parked in Lompoc, California, and considering its overall condition, with a running engine and everything else, you should be able to drive it home on its wheels. This means you wouldn't have to cover the shipping costs, keeping the Bel Air as expensive as it gets.
There’s no word on any paperwork, such as the original build sheet and everything else, but you’ll be getting a title anyway.

New Hot Wheels Pop Culture Set Brings Jerry Smith, Doctor Doom and Deadpool Together
11 photos
Photo: Diecast Wheels
Not having the Facebook app on my phone anymore is mostly a blessing. There’s only one downside to it all: I have limited access to my local Hot Wheels collector’s group. And that means I can be quite slow in reacting to certain opportunities on the market.
One of my favorite dealers these days is a guy who keeps bringing in old gems from the ‘90s, and he just posted 50 new cars recently. Most of them are Ferraris, with prices ranging between $10 to $20. These are all Mainlines, and he sold a few by the time I could sign up for anything. But I’m pretty sure I have all I need for a Ferrari -themed unboxing coming in December the latest!
The guy also had an older Star Wars-related model I had been thinking about for a while: a Spoiler Sport paying tribute to Darth Vader! I’ve already unboxed the Dream Van XGW Panel (Princess Leia) and the Volkswagen Drag Truck (Luke Skywalker) from that 2015 Pop Culture mix. And I’m thrilled to be able to explore this line’s history.
The future is somewhat exciting, too, and I just saw the first preview of what’s likely coming up in Mix 2 for 2027! You may have already seen Jerry’s Station Wagon about two weeks ago, when we also got a glimpse of the next Car Culture mix for next year. But Mr. Lambert’s video at the time didn’t include a shot of the blister card.
We can see Morty’s dad shrugging his shoulders like he typically does, just outside the Smith residence with Rick’s garage in the background. I’d almost buy two of these collectibles, just so I could keep one carded! With a bit of effort, I’m sure I could go after all of Mattel’s Rick & Morty collectibles, it might be an exciting side quest!
Jerry’s Station is the only brand-new casting in this mix, but there’s more to the story still. Take, for instance, the Hiway Hauler. While Doctor Doom looks familiar to me, I’m not nearly as familiar with him as I am with the previous theme in this mix. I guess watching Avengers: Doomsday would be one way to deal with that “problem”, but I’m more than happy sticking with Godzilla Minus Zero and Dune this year.
The Pizza Planet Truck has been around since 2019, and Mattel just used it as a The Good Dinosaur collectible earlier this year. I doubt the new variation will be successful, unless more people will become Toy Story fans until then. The Ford GT looks like an enticing proposal even though this Gran Turismo theme is by no means a premiere.
I believe this “new” iteration might be identical to the 2016 Hot Wheels Entertainment release, so it’s not all bad once you realize that came out a decade ago. I didn’t think much of Deadpool’s Scooter when I bought it, then hated it for not having a kickstand, only to realize it can balance itself without one. His Chimichanga Truck is quite a bit nicer by comparison, and I’m definitely getting one!

This UK-Built Camper Van Cleverly Makes Room for a Family of Six Without Sacrificing Comfort
14 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions
What does it take to be able to take your family on van life adventures? I'd say it takes a well-thought-out build that can offer proper comfort for everyone involved – that's the type of project I'd like to share with you today.
This rig is based on a MAN TGE and was brought to life by a skilled team of people over at Ashben Conversions. This Sheffield, UK-based company specializes in high-quality camper vans and motorhomes tailored to individual customer needs.
The customer, Harry, requested a setup that could accommodate his partner and their four kids. As you can imagine, fitting six people in a van is a challenge, but Ashben Conversions delivered.
As always, let's start by taking a look at the van's exterior. For starters, it rides on Rogue Alloy Wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich all-terrain tires.
The exterior upgrade that turns the van family-friendly is the Atek pop-top roof tent. What I mean is that it offers a sleeping arrangement for two of the kids. The tent is made out of three pieces of fiberglass and can incorporate a mattress of up to 120 x 200 centimeters (47 x 78 inches).
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions It comes with three zipped windows and can be accessed only from inside the van through a large pass-through in the ceiling. What's more, on top of the tent, you'll come across a 300 W solar array.
Other notable mods are power and water hookups, a Thule Omnistor awning with a built-in LED light, and a set of flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van's width to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south.
This van's CGL side pods are paint matched to the body and come with small windows with sliding screens.
Inside is where the biggest transformation happened. The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for laminated cabinetry with a dark grey grain finish, walls upholstered in grey Alcantara leather, and a matching ceiling with three recessed LED light strips. The look is complemented by white solid surface countertops and some black accents, like the seat upholstery and the sink faucet.
The front part of the interior can be used as a seating area. First, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases that allow you to turn them around to face the back of the van.
Second, the rest of the family can sit further back in another arrangement. It comprises two dual bench seats facing one another, with a large Lagun table in the middle. The seats in the cabin also get a Lagun table.
The setup is not only ideal for enjoying meals or playing some games, but it's also where the family's four kids can be safely and comfortably accommodated when the van is in motion. Above, you'll find two decently sized cabinets and the tent pass-through I mentioned earlier.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions This is also where two of the kids will be sleeping. Setting up a small bed here is quick and easy – you just have to remove the Lagun table leg, drop the tabletop between the benches, and rearrange the cushions.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side, right beside the sliding door. It features a deep stainless steel sink, a two-burner induction stovetop, a Dometic fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, and a microwave oven.
Six drawers and a cabinet underneath the sink are available in the kitchen. A bit further back on the same side, you get a floor-to-ceiling unit integrating a closet with hanging space and some shelves.
Opposite the kitchen, you'll discover what's generally one of the most wanted camper van facilities: a bathroom, hidden behind a tall conventional door. It boasts a bench toilet, a shower with a handheld wand, and a small cabinet.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions The rear part of the living space is reserved for relaxing and sleeping, as it's taken up by a fixed bed arrangement with a double-sized mattress. Since the bed is positioned a bit higher up, you can use a small ladder to make it easier to climb into bed. The bedroom also offers four overhead cabinets (two on each side), charging points, and two reading lights.
Finally, the space underneath the bed was turned into a garage, which is accessible from both inside and outside the van.
The garage offers abundant room for storage and accommodates the rig's utility systems inside boxes on the sides.
Power is on the left – the electrical system's highlights are a 460 Ah Fogstar battery and a 3,000 W Victron inverter. Three charging sources allow you to keep the battery topped off: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank, and an outdoor shower connection.
There are two other important systems that make this rig capable of adventuring in any season: a Truma Saphir A/C unit and a Truma D4E Combi boiler that provides both heated air and hot water.
The rear doors are equipped with gas struts that make it easier for you to open them. They also prevent the doors from slamming shut or hitting the sides of the vehicle.
All in all, Ashben Conversions really pushed this MAN TGE-based conversion to its limits. It turned it into a family-friendly mobile home that not only has room for six people, but also packs all they need to be able to enjoy comfort on the road.

1968 Chevrolet Caprice Station Wagon Sells for Record Price
16 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
When it comes to classic cars sold at public auctions, we usually report records set by iconic models, mainly from the high-performance and luxury segments. That's where the big bucks are. But from time to time I like to check the more mundane cars, mostly to observe market trends. Well, I just learned that the 1968 Chevrolet Caprice is now a potentially more valuable classic.
Introduced in 1966, the Caprice was Chevrolet's range-topping model. It sat above the Impala and competed against the Ford LTD, Plymouth Fury VIP, and AMC Ambassador DLP. It had a more upscale interior and a flashier exterior. Sixty years later, the first-generation Caprice is a popular choice for lowrider builders and restomodders, but it's not a highly collectible classic.
While some examples have sold for over $50,000 and even reached into $80,000 territory, they're still far from fetching six-figures (which contemporary Impalas and Corvettes do). In fact, the average auction price for a first-gen Caprice in excellent condition is still under $25,000. And that's precisely why a 1968 Caprice selling for over $80,000 is pretty big news.
It happened at Mecum's Las Vegas 2026 auction on November 13, where a station wagon changed hands for $82,500. Mind you, this isn't an expensive custom fitted with a modern powertrain, but a frame-off restoration completed with new-old-stock components. This thing is as factory-correct as they get.
It looks like it just rolled off the showroom floor, sporting impeccable paint, shiny chrome trim, and outstanding simulated wood panels. It has a matching three-row interior and still relies on the original 327-cubic-inch (5.4-liter) V8 engine.
The price may seem a bit surprising given the lack of a big-block mill, but I should point out that this Caprice is loaded with options and accessories—over 40, to be exact. The list includes the rare stainless upholstery trim, AC, power everything, cruise control , multi-plex stereo, tissue dispenser, and a roof rack. It also has the rare hideaway headlamps.
There is an exception to the factory-correct status I mentioned above: The ad says that the Caprice has a "modified suspension with front and rear air bags."
The selling price makes this station wagon by far the most expensive 1968 Caprice ever sold at public auction; it smashed the previous record by nearly $30K. Up until now, the benchmark was held by a two-door hardtop that sold for $53,900 in early 2023. The same car traded for over $40,000 in 2022 and 2023 again. Before that, the record belonged to a different station wagon that changed hands for $38,000 in 2019.
At the same time, this grocery-getter is now the most expensive first-generation Caprice ever sold at public auction. It smashed a record previously set by a 1966 two-door coupe at $71,500 in 2016.
What's your take on this auction? Is the first-gen Caprice on its way to becoming a more valuable classic, or is this wagon an exception? Would you pay over $80,000 for a long-roof Chevy?

2028 Lexus IS Wagon Dressed in Black Looks Like a Digital Postcard For the Return of the Mighty V8
9 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
Although Lexus feels like it’s among the few carmakers that don't actively seek to abandon the passenger car sector in the United States, the offer has been restricted for the 2027 model year to just the compact IS executive car and the eighth generation of the larger ES – offered as a hybrid or EV.
However, thanks to a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators who stopped for a moment from dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, we are here specifically to discuss the long-lived Lexus IS , with its third-generation version having arrived way back in 2013.
It underwent a series of facelifts – in 2017, 2020, and most recently in 2025 when it was refreshed with a redesigned front end, new rear spoiler, and a completely overhauled interior, among other things. That was a great idea, breathing new life into a great compact executive sedan. Alas, for the US market, the range was restricted to the RWD and AWD options and the IS 350 model.
The compact sedan has endured into the 2027 model year, too, and now alongside the F Sport Design and F Sport models there’s also an IS 350 F Sport Special Appearance Package, with all three of them sharing the same powerplant – the ubiquitous 3.5-liter V6 packing 311 hp and enabling a sprint to 60 mph in just 5.9 seconds. But what if that’s not enough?
Some folks, most likely, lament the absence of the mighty V8, of course. Others, like Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, who thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the Lexus IS – all over again, want more body style options.
This pixel master, immediately after the latest refresh, came up with the idea to bring back the SportCross body style – the station wagon. The five-door practical version of the Lexus IS was shown in silver with matching Y-spoke alloy wheels and red brake calipers, so we immediately thought that the 5.0-liter 2UR-GSE V8 engine with 472 horsepower and 395 lb-ft of torque would also fit like a glove in there to give the BMW M3 Touring a run for its CGI money.
Earlier this year, the CGI expert went back to the drawing board and showed us the Lexus IS with a station wagon body style dressed in orange and featuring dark-concave alloy wheels, raising our craving for the V8 powertrain to spectacular levels. Oh, and wait, because that wasn’t all.
Instead, a few weeks later the author also cooked up a nice Lexus IS Coupe variant that would look quite at home alongside the sedan and the unofficial, hypothetical station wagon design project. Of course, it would pack both the V6 and V8 options, too. Now, as it turns out, the imagined Lexus IS SportCross is back for the late-fall season and a potential 2028 model year, this time around dressed completely in black and with matching or contrasting black or silver aftermarket alloy wheels.
So, what do you think - yay or nay? Compact but Comfy: The NTR2X Offroad Travel Trailer Promises Total Comfort
12 photos
Photo: Hunter Nature
We shouldn't judge books – let alone travel trailers – by their appearance, and this compact and relatively lightweight caravan is almost daring you to do it just to show you how wrong it would be. This is the NTR2X, a family-friendly offroad travel trailer designed for all kinds of adventures.
The NTR2X is the smallest of its kind: it's the smallest entry in the series of offroad trailers from Hunter Nature. That name probably means nothing to you, and that's mostly because they're based out of Turkey though shipping their products all over Europe, albeit in small numbers.
Hunter Nature is a regular presence at trade events and has even made international headlines before, with units that folded out to offer more living space at camp, as was the case with the Raptor , itself a new development of an older concept that also went viral. They've been making travel trailers since 2019, all of them by European standards, motivated mostly by the desire to be the sole manufacturer of truly offroad caravans in Europe.
They're currently offering five floorplans under the NTR name, with the NTR2X being the smallest. As its name hints, it's meant to be a couple's unit that offers sleeping for just two people, but it can actually be optioned to accommodate an entire family of four. You'll have to spend a bit more for that, of course, to add a single or double bed in the roof.
Photo: Hunter Nature Like its bigger sibling, the NTR4X we saw earlier this week, the NTR2X comes with a pop-up roof that was designed specifically for this series. Unlike its bigger sibling, it features a wedge-shaped tent with a hard cover and canvas walls, and a rear entrance.
You can still use the trailer without the tent section opened, especially if you want to make use of its insulation for some wintertime adventures. On hotter days, you can open the roof for extra ventilation, in addition to getting to full standing height.
This model is designed for shorter trips on road or off of it, at the campsite or not. The upside to a much smaller footprint and a lighter weight is that you can tow it without your daily driver without needing to upgrade from your regular B Category driving license.
Photo: Hunter Nature For a weekend warrior or the occasional adventurer looking simply to spend some quality time with the fam or friends but without much hassle, the NTR2X seems like the perfect solution . You get a "comfortable camping experience" with no headaches, so what's not to like about it?
Construction is with a steel chassis and a full aluminum body, like in the bigger models. The NTR2X rides on a single axle with independent spring suspension and AL-KO stabilizers, and comes with an electric entry step, awning-style large windows with integrated blinds and flyscreens, and prep for two kitchens.
It also seems to offer an indoor bathroom in a small cubicle, which could be either a full wet bath or a space for a cassette toilet. Hunter Nature doesn't offer clear details about that, but they do say that you can add an outdoor shower as an option.
Photo: Hunter Nature The NTR2X comes in at 4.5 meters (14.7 feet) of total length, with just 3 meters (9.8f eet) in the body and 1.88 meters (6.1 feet) of overall width. It travels at 2.25 meters (7.3 feet) in height and reaches 3.11 meters (10 feet) at its highest rear point at camp, when you open up the roof with just one hand.
Inside, you have storage and the supposed bathroom cubicle, a small galley kitchen off the side, and a U-shaped dinette with an adjustable table that also helps to convert this seating area into a double bed. It's a small camper so features and amenities will be limited – and relative to the size of the footprint.
That said, like with its bigger brother, Hunter Nature strives to create a cozy, welcoming, and highly functional space . You get all-aluminum cabinetry and composite materials, with some focus on aesthetics and lots of attention to durability and functionality.
Photo: Hunter Nature Options include an outdoor kitchen setup that would render the indoor galley obsolete except for brewing coffee in really bad weather. Where the indoor one has a single-burner and a tiny tap combo unit, the exterior one features two burners, a slide-out tray for a griddle or additional worktop space, a sink, and some storage. A cooler box on a slider tray tucks neatly into the box at the front of the trailer.
Standard features include a 230 or 340W solar panel on the roof, a 100 or 150Ah lithium battery, an 80-liter (21-gallon) tank for freshwater, and a 30-liter (8-gallon) one for gray.
Hunter Nature mentions a weight of 790-900 kg (1,741-1,984 lbs), which is probably empty weight depending on equipment. Maximum permissible weight is probably 1,000-1,100 kg (2,204-2,425 lbs), so you could still tow it without upgrading your driving license.
Photo: Hunter Nature The manufacturer doesn't list a starting price for the model, but the bigger NTR4X we looked at earlier on sells for around £55,000 in the UK (approximately €65,800 or $73,000 at the current exchange rate). It's not cheap, but it promises to do things cheap caravans could never.

A Bunkroom Inside an Elegant Apartment on Wheels: Meet the 2027 WestWyn 38DB Fifth Wheel RV
10 photos
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter
To anyone thinking that family-friendly RV-ing has to mean cramped spaces, no attention to aesthetics, or no sense of privacy, Recreation by Design has one thing to say. The WestWyn 38DB is that hold-my-beer-kind of response.
WestWyn is a name even less known than Recreation by Design, the manufacturing company. Recreation by Design is a family-owned manufacturer that's been around for long enough to have actual credibility, and a catalog impressive enough to attract attention. The latter recently got even better, with the debut of the company's first-ever fifth wheel series, WestWyn.
We actually had a look at the flagship model earlier this week. Called the WestWyn 37R , it's a very elegant and very well built couple's rig, designed and built to be different in every aspect that matters. Recreation by Design handles almost everything in-house, from the heavy-duty steel frame construction to the cabinetry, and that means that they deliver on every promise they make.
The WestWyn 38DB is the family-friendly version of the 37R. It's a bunkhouse model that offers sleeping for three kids, the parents, and two more guests that can crash on the sleeper sofa in the open-plan living room. Unlike other family-friendly fifth wheelers, this one offers actual privacy inside, solid quality, and the aesthetics of a large city apartment.
Photo: Recreation by Design It's a must see – and see it you can in the video tour available at the bottom of the page.
The 38DB is built on a heavy-duty steel chassis with tandem 7,000-lb axles with 17.5-inch aluminum wheels, J-rated tires, and MORryde CRE3000 suspension. It's built with Azdel sidewalls, a fully insulated floor, an enclosed and insulated underbelly, a walkable PVC roof (including on the two slide-outs), and a molded fiberglass front cap with automotive paint.
Recreation by Design describes it as a year-round, full-time RV , so it doesn't just look like a (very fancy) house: it's also built like one.
Photo: Recreation by Design While this floorplan shares an identical front end with the 37R, it's actually a bit longer, coming in at 40 feet(12 meters). It's still 13.4 feet (4 meters) tall and 100 inches (254 inches) wide, but it has a single super-slide in the living room space and the same teeny-tiny slide-out in the bedroom, for the unique closet with sliding doors.
Like most fifth wheelers out there, the 38DB has the bedroom and bathroom on the upper deck, both of which are the same as in the 37R, so quite nice on the eyes and packed with functionality.
Recreation by Design uses a somewhat typical fifth wheel design but then reinvents everything else about it, creating spaces that are different from anything else on the market right now. The bedroom remains a solid example in this sense, with the bunkroom a close second.
Photo: Recreation by Design In the bedroom, you get a queen bed with a backlit headboard where you'd normally find a windshield in other fifth wheelers, and a closet in the small slide-out. The bed sits lower to the floor than normal, which creates a sense of space that you wouldn't have had otherwise, but it still features storage underneath.
Not that you really need it, since options are plenty inside the bedroom: his and hers closets on either side, matching nightstands with drawers, and a closet at the foot of the bed with adjustable shelves and prep for a washer and dryer. Then, there's the closet in the slide-out, with large sliding doors and extendable hangers.
The bunkroom is also different than most fifth wheel bunkrooms out there. Using an L-shaped sleeping arrangement, Recreation by Design is able to squeeze in three beds and plenty of usable storage space, while also making sure the three kids who do sleep in here also get privacy thanks to a pocket door.
Photo: Recreation by Design Entrance is done into the dining space, occupied by an L-shaped bench seating with an adjustable table and some storage. From here, you step into the living room space, where you find a sleeper sofa facing a wall-mounted TV and an electric fireplace.
This entertainment center continues into the kitchen, which is also L-shaped. It's more compact than the one in the 37R floorplan but it still integrates residential appliances, including a large Furrion fridge and freezer side-by-side and a dishwasher. Families traveling with kids would expect nothing less but a fully functional kitchen space, especially in an RV marketed as suitable for full-time living.
Standard features include solid surface counters throughout, even in the bathroom, stainless steel undermounted sinks, soft close hinges on all opening doors of the cabinetry, and pocket screw drawers made of solid wood.
Photo: Recreation by Design Cabinetry is built in-house and offered in a selection of colors, but Recreation by Design opted for high-gloss upper cabinets, light gray lower cabinets, and all-black upholstery for the display unit. The contrast creates a striking, modern style that remains cozy and inviting.
Also standard are frameless windows with integrated blackouts, a power awning, a 35,000-BTU furnace, two Furrion ACs (an 18,000-BTU unit with a heat pump and an 8,000-BTU one for the bedroom), a Fogatti on-demand water heater, and JBL sound inside and out. Like in the other floorplan, all the controls are behind a sliding door on the wall, with sensor lighting and a design that betrays the kind of attention to detail this manufacturer puts into everything they do.
This fifth wheeler comes with a 71-gallon (268-liter) tank for freshwater, a 90-gallon (340-liter) one for gray, and a 50-gallon (189-liter) one for black, all of them heated. It features prep for Starlink, 650W of solar, and a backup camera, and comes with six-point hydraulic auto-leveling and a Gen-Y pinbox.
Photo: Recreation by Design Recreation by Design notes that the full list of specs is pending. The unit shown below is a functional prototype, so some things might change by the time the floorplan goes into production. When it does reach dealers, it's expected to do so with an asking price between $90,000 and $105,000.
